title: Best practices - Pedantic model on router vs argments?
body: ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python ## Example 1 : pydantic model directly passed as an argument ## @village_router.post( "/villages", response_model=VillageOut, response_model_exclude_none=True ) async def village_create( village: VillageCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db), current_user: User = Depends(get_current_active_user), ): """ Create a new village """ # Ensure the authenticated user is the owner village.owner_id = current_user.id try: new_village = create_user_village(db, village) return new_village except Exception as e: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e)) ## Example 2 : build the pydantic object inside the router ## @village_router.post( "/villages", response_model=VillageOut, response_model_exclude_none=True ) async def village_create( village_name: str = Body(...), x_coordinate: int = Body(...), y_coordinate: int = Body(...), db: Session = Depends(get_db), current_user: User = Depends(get_current_active_user), ): village = VillageCreate(name=village_name, x=x_coordinate, y=y_coordinate) village.owner_id = current_user.id try: new_village = create_user_village(db, village) return new_village except Exception as e: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e)) ``` ### Description I am quite new to API development and I am just wondering what is the best practice for my case or in general. I am trying to build a robust and well-written full stack app where my client is a react application but we may have more clients on the long run. I have 3 mains folders: routers, schemas and models. The router is the entry point of the API, schemas are my Pydantic model mostly used for validation and models my tables representations. I have one API endpoint, a POST endpoint to create a new village. To create a new village, we need to know 3 informations: village name, x and y coordinates. Should I pass directly a CreateVillage pydantic model as an argument to my router endpoint vs 3 individual parameters (name, x and y) and then build the CreateVillage object within the router method code? I am currently using the first method but when I am looking at my swagger, I don't see any arguments and everything is within the request body. If I use the second method, 3 clear input parameters will be showed on the swagger. What's the ideal practice? ### Operating System macOS ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version 0.95.0 ### Pydantic Version 2.10.6 ### Python Version 3.8 ### Additional Context _No response_

First Check

 I added a very descriptive title here.
 I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
 I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
 I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
 I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
 I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to Pydantic.
 I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to Swagger UI.
 I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to ReDoc.

Commit to Help

 I commit to help with one of those options 👆

Example Code
## Example 1 : pydantic model directly passed as an argument ##

@village_router.post(
    "/villages", response_model=VillageOut, response_model_exclude_none=True
)
async def village_create(
    village: VillageCreate,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_active_user),
):
    """
    Create a new village
    """
    # Ensure the authenticated user is the owner
    village.owner_id = current_user.id

    try:
        new_village = create_user_village(db, village)
        return new_village
    except Exception as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))


## Example 2 : build the pydantic object inside the router ##

@village_router.post(
    "/villages", response_model=VillageOut, response_model_exclude_none=True
)
async def village_create(
    village_name: str = Body(...),
    x_coordinate: int = Body(...),
    y_coordinate: int = Body(...),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_active_user),
):

    village = VillageCreate(name=village_name, x=x_coordinate, y=y_coordinate)
    village.owner_id = current_user.id

    try:
        new_village = create_user_village(db, village)
        return new_village
    except Exception as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
Description
I am quite new to API development and I am just wondering what is the best practice for my case or in general. I am trying to build a robust and well-written full stack app where my client is a react application but we may have more clients on the long run.
I have 3 mains folders: routers, schemas and models. The router is the entry point of the API, schemas are my Pydantic model mostly used for validation and models my tables representations.
I have one API endpoint, a POST endpoint to create a new village. To create a new village, we need to know 3 informations: village name, x and y coordinates.
Should I pass directly a CreateVillage pydantic model as an argument to my router endpoint vs 3 individual parameters (name, x and y) and then build the CreateVillage object within the router method code?
I am currently using the first method but when I am looking at my swagger, I don't see any arguments and everything is within the request body. If I use the second method, 3 clear input parameters will be showed on the swagger.
What's the ideal practice?

answer.body:
HI @Pierre-Alexandre35, 
The best practice for your case is to pass the model as an argument, like you're doing in "Example 1".

This is suggested in the docs https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/body/#declare-it-as-a-parameter and you can see there the resulting swagger, too. 

See also this related linting rule: https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/too-many-arguments/
